expectations.text: Refuses to print a bare meeting number in the prospectus with no criteria and no stated make-good
expectations.evidence: "Do not print '20 guaranteed meetings...' in the prospectus. It's a bare number with no criteria and no stated make-good"

expectations.text: Explains the failure of a bare guaranteed count: it can be satisfied by filling slots with whoever is free, leaving the sponsor worse off than if nothing had been promised
expectations.evidence: The explanation given is that there are no criteria, no make-good, and that "senior" can't be verified. It never says a bare count can be met with whoever is free.

expectations.text: Names a best-efforts target as the default commitment shape, with criteria written down even there
expectations.evidence: It recommends "Contract: recommended shape (guaranteed count with criteria)" and treats best-efforts as the "fallback shape".

expectations.text: Allows promotion to a guaranteed count with criteria, keyed to the contracted number and to the opt-in profile data being good enough to verify the criteria
expectations.evidence: "If that pool is clearly large enough for 20 accepted meetings, the guaranteed shape below is defensible."

expectations.text: Requires each criterion to be evidenced by a self-entered profile field, and a criterion with no evidence route to be given a field or dropped
expectations.evidence: "Evidence. The attendee's self-entered role field and 'currently evaluating' field. No inferred seniority"

expectations.text: Defines what does not count toward the 20, such as a counterpart from the sponsor's own company, an existing relationship, a meeting booked but not held, or a substitute person
expectations.evidence: "Anyone from Kelvin's own company... existing relationship... booked but not held... substitute person."

expectations.text: Names who decides a borderline case and by when, before the event
expectations.evidence: "Name one OrbitConf person who decides, and a date for the decision that falls before the event"

expectations.text: Requires a defined make-good chosen at commitment time that the organizer can still fund after the event has ended
expectations.evidence: "Choose one now. Don't leave it open." and "You must still have the cash after the event."

expectations.text: Rules out a talk slot, judging seat, or share of the agenda as a make-good, because sponsorship buys access and never program influence
expectations.evidence: "Speaking, judging or agenda access... sponsorship never buys influence over the program."

expectations.text: Rules out attendee data as a make-good
expectations.evidence: "Attendee names or data. This breaks the consent each attendee gave"

expectations.text: Routes drafting of the actual clause wording elsewhere, keeping only the commitment's shape in this design
expectations.evidence: "Hand these sentences to whoever drafts the clause (event-sponsor-agreement). They set the shape, not the legal wording"

expectations.text: States that delivery against the promise is reported per sponsor, never averaged across sponsors
expectations.evidence: "It's tracked per sponsor, never as an average."

expectations.text: Does not state any fill rate, acceptance rate, or no-show percentage in support of the guarantee
expectations.evidence: "I stated no meeting length, slot count, fill rate or no-show percentage anywhere above."

expectations.text: Refuses to print a bare meeting number in the prospectus with no criteria and no stated make-good
expectations.evidence: "Don't print '20 guaranteed meetings with senior platform engineers' as written." The criteria and remedy are supplied.
